theme: for people who wake up already tense about the day
title: Five Breaths Before the Day Begins: 8 Minutes
spotifyTitle: Morning Meditation: Five Breaths to Start the Day Calm
subtitle: A short morning practice for putting the day down before it starts
insightTimerDescription:
A gentle eight minute morning practice for anyone who wakes up already tense about the day ahead. Five slow breaths, one ordinary thing to be glad of, and one simple intention to carry with you.

Use it first thing, sitting up in bed or in a chair by the window, before you look at your phone. It works best as a daily habit, so come back to it tomorrow morning and the morning after.

Go gently into your day.

theme: for people who lie awake with a busy mind
title: Yoga Nidra to Put the Day Down: 22 Minutes
spotifyTitle: Yoga Nidra for Sleep: Put the Day Down and Drift Off
subtitle: Rest the body, quiet the mind, and let sleep come by itself
insightTimerDescription:
A slow, gentle yoga nidra for the end of the day, for anyone who lies awake with a busy mind. You will be guided through the whole body, a simple wish, an easy breath count and a few quiet pictures, until there is nothing left to do but rest.

Listen in bed with the lights low, lying on your back or however you sleep best. There is no bell at the end and no need to wake up, so let it carry you into sleep. It works well as a nightly practice.

Sleep well.

theme: for nights when the mind will not settle
title: A Long, Slow Way Down to Sleep: 45 Minutes
spotifyTitle: Sleep Meditation: A Long, Slow Journey Down to Deep Sleep
subtitle: A quiet lane, a sheltered bay, and a boat that rocks you to sleep
insightTimerDescription:
A long guided journey into sleep for nights when the mind will not settle. After a slow count down and a gentle softening of the body, you will walk down a quiet lane to a sheltered bay and drift in a little boat under the stars, while soft music carries on long after my voice has faded.

Put it on once you are in bed, with the lights out and the volume low. There is no bell and nothing at the end to wake you, so you can simply fall asleep partway through. Many people use a track like this every night.

Rest well.

theme: setting down a worry or hurt you have carried too long
title: Set Down What You've Been Carrying: 10 Minutes
spotifyTitle: Letting Go Meditation: Set Down What You've Been Carrying
subtitle: Ten minutes by a slow river
insightTimerDescription:
A ten minute practice for letting go of something you have been carrying for too long: a worry, a hurt, or a weight you can't quite name. You will notice where it sits in your body, breathe with it, set it down on a slow river, and rest in the space it leaves behind.

Sit or lie somewhere quiet where you won't be disturbed. Use it whenever something feels heavy, or practise it daily for a week and notice what changes. If it comes back, simply come back to the river.

Go gently.

theme: for the moments when you are hard on yourself
title: A Hand on Your Own Heart: 5 Minutes
spotifyTitle: Self Compassion Meditation: 5 Minutes of Kindness for Yourself
subtitle: Five minutes to be on your own side
insightTimerDescription:
A short practice of kindness for the moments when you are being hard on yourself, or simply having a difficult day. With a hand on your heart, you will name what is hard and offer yourself the words you would give a good friend.

It takes five minutes, so you can use it anywhere: at your desk, in the car before you go in, or last thing at night. It is most powerful as a small daily habit.

Be kind to yourself today.

theme: for anxious moments when the mind is racing
title: Back to Solid Ground: 10 Minutes
spotifyTitle: Meditation for Anxiety: Back to Solid Ground in 10 Minutes
subtitle: For when worry won't let go
insightTimerDescription:
A steady ten minute practice for anxious moments, when your mind is racing or your chest feels tight. You will feel your feet on the ground, settle your senses, slow down with long breaths out, and make a little room for the feeling instead of fighting it.

Use it whenever worry builds, sitting or lying down, with your eyes open or closed. Come back to it as often as you need. Practising on calmer days too helps it come more easily when you need it most.

You are not alone in this.
